pr_title: Round managedFields times to the nearest second before sorting
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug
/sig api-machinery
/wg apply
/cc @lavalamp @liggitt 
/priority important-soon

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #88031

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```
pr_comments: were there more than one place we did sorting? would it also make sense to try to resolve this issue where we originate manager timestamps by setting up in-memory times truncated to a second?
@liggitt there was another place where we sort but this is the final sort before serializing, so the earlier one doesn't matter
I switched the other sort implementation for consistency
The fact that we have to fix this twice is quite concerning to me.
It'd be better if we truncated when setting these.

> It'd be better if we truncated when setting these.

I agree, no one should have to care about these "details".

@apelisse I'm not sure if it would be better to truncate when setting them, since then anyone setting these would have to care about these details. Maybe we could do both? truncate when setting them, and when comparing
The core of the problem is that serialize/deserialize doesn't roundtrip (not bijective)? There's clearly a bug with our type ...
@apelisse I guess that problem exists in metav1.Time

/lgtm
/approve

This is better than the existing code (avoids allocation), if you want to improve it further you can always send another PR.

issue_context.title: managedFields updates for no-op writes
comments:
> diff 1.yaml 2.yaml shows the kubectl and kube-controller-manager managed field sets swapped order

Can you print the before/after fieldmanager? I can't quite figure out what the actual values are.
The code that sorts these lists is located [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/fieldmanager/internal/managedfields.go#L189-L215)

updated to unified diff and attached:

- [1.txt](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/4187705/1.txt)
- [2.txt](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/4187706/2.txt)
- [3.txt](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/4187708/3.txt)
- [watch.txt](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/4187709/watch.txt)
If you explicitly set the field manager to something unique, does it happen every time?
hm, no, it's definitely an ordering swap
1.txt is not sorted properly, since `kube-controller-manager` should come before `kubectl`.

We seem to also sort it in a second place: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/574acbe31025bd7a298eae5dc72b0256a7a9b11a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/fieldmanager/capmanagers.go#L80-L91
Theory: the first time it goes through, the time is accurate to the nanosecond; the second time, it's accurate to the second
Yeah OK I'm pretty sure that's it, both times are the same second. Serialization drops the fractional part.

review_comments: This sort routine doesn't actually matter for this bug, since it combines the oldest ones, it's fine if new ones have extra precision.
